title: Lumbar lordosis range of extension by age (Epionics, 429 volunteers)

quantity.name: lumbar range of extension
quantity.definition: Change of lumbar lordosis angle (sum of segments lordotic in standing) between upright standing and maximal flexion (RoM flexion) or maximal extension (RoM extension); the paper's wording ('difference of the lordosis angle at maximum flexion and maximum extension respectively') is read as each relative to standing, consistent with Dreischarf 2014 on the same device.

source.authors: Consmuller T, Rohlmann A, Weinland D, Druschel C, Duda GN, Taylor WR
source.sample: asymptomatic volunteers aged 20-75 (no LBP in 6 months, no spinal surgery); age classes 20-35 (n=189), 36-50 (n=146), 51-75 (n=94); no BMI exclusion

protocol.summary: Lumbar lordosis RoM in extension by age class, 429 asymptomatic adults, Epionics SPINE (Table 1).
how_to_use: Use as the lumbar contribution at maximal extension for a subject of matching age class.
Age reduces lumbar RoM (flexion 54.0 -> 45.1 deg; extension 29.7 -> 19.5 deg from 20-35 to 51-75 y).
This sample includes BMI>26 subjects and fully contains the Dreischarf 2014 and Pries 2015 samples: prefer those for sex-specific values and do not pool.

measurement.device: Epionics SPINE strain-gauge strips 5 cm lateral of midline, lowest segment at PSIS; 50 Hz
measurement.task: 5 x maximal flexion and 5 x maximal extension at preferred speed

protocol.notes: Same Charite/Epionics volunteer database: Consmuller 2012 = all 429; Dreischarf 2014 = 323 with BMI<26; Pries 2015 = 309 (BMI<26 and valid sacral accelerometer). Do not pool these as independent samples.

extraction.check_notes: '6' in text extraction is the +- glyph; values re-read from layout text of Table 1.

pass_rule.rule: input data – not graded; use for robustness checks
